description:
## Question

The cosine top-k workload needs `[f32]` and PCM mixing needs `[i16]`/`[i32]` (see "Choose the target workload set"). Elixir has no f32 and no fixed-width integers, so these are divergence questions: when a kernel reads an element, what type does it get (f32 promoted to f64? i16 widened to i64?), what happens on a write that doesn't fit (raise, saturate, wrap: PCM clipping is saturation), is f32 arithmetic ever done in f32, and how does an Elixir caller build and read these arrays? The answer must fit the one rule.

comments.text: Per 'What is the one rule a kernel author keeps in their head?' (defk-dtw.7): [T] is a binary of native-endian T; reads follow the bitstring match (f32 widens to f64 with Elixir's rounding, narrow ints widen to i64); a write that doesn't fit its type raises (a limit; Elixir would wrap or store inf). PCM clipping is an explicit min/max.

title: What do narrow element types ([f32], [i16], [i32]) mean in a kernel?
